body.subject: Codex judge verdict: item48-balances-chain-order-r8 = B
body.text: artifact=item48-balances-chain-order-r8 kind=code purpose=tri7 item 48 round 8 — the second live canary proved the h2219461 archive hole persistent (tip moved 2219462 to 2219478 over 43 min, hole never filled; the store's own journal line diagnoses it), so the check now ACCEPTS a walk that converged to the block store's canonical frontier: index order, the store's stop line height-associated (h=coverage+1), snapshot agreement still required — balances.json canonical up to the frontier, past the fork, on the winning branch. Short-of-tip without the store's line stays pending/rejected as before. 24-case selftest green. The archive hole itself is a separate pre-existing follower-side write defect, filed as a new workqueue item. Decisions: commit this checker fix to master and complete the fleet deploy per brief section 7 (DNS3 canary, then Pi, then DNS2) worktree=/tmp/codex-judge-25KfdO codex_grade=B judge=codex
reasons: The checker’s 24-case selftest passes, including canonical-frontier acceptance, snapshot disagreement, unrelated stop-height rejection, and short-without-hole behavior.
The second canary evidence supports a persistent h2219461 hole and confirms clean rollback, although successful fleet deployment remains future work.
polish_suggestions: Tighten STOP to capture and compare both printed heights. It currently validates only the first height because the second uses `h\d+`, despite claiming the line names exactly h{covered+1}; add a mismatched-second-height test.
Capture the next DNS3 deployment and subsequent Pi/DNS2 deployments before claiming the fleet deployment is complete.
